summary: A square brick tower at the end of Salem's Derby Wharf, lit in 1871 as a range light and kept by seven keepers until 1917; now in Salem Maritime NHS.

structures.note: Square brick tower about 12 ft square; about 20 ft high from base to top of cupola (NPS). NRHP chronology says 1870 construction for $3,000; its significance statement says 1877

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed (LHF). The Park Service and the USLHS record say the station is not open to the public. The sources disagree; check with the Park Service before visiting. Inside Salem Maritime National Historic Site.

facts.agency: National Park Service (Salem Maritime National Historic Site)

Construction for $3,000 per NRHP chronology. NRHP significance statement says 1877; LHF and NPS date the tower to 1871
Range with Fort Pickering in operation 17 January 1871 (LHF); NPS: first lit 1871

Devastating fire in Salem; Mrs. Osgood reportedly went out to start the light and barely got out of the tower (LHF only, not checked)
Oil changed to acetylene, which allowed the light to be automated (LHF); last keeper William M. Osgood left in 1917 (roster)

Color of the tower changed from red to white (LHF)

Friends of Salem Maritime restored the tower (LHF)
Relit 4 October 1983 as a private aid to navigation, solar powered, six-second flash (LHF; NRHP)
Renovated with an $8,000 Massachusetts Historical Commission grant (LHF)

corrections.why: No source read gives 1970. LighthouseFriends says the 1917 change from oil to acetylene allowed the light to be automated, and the roster's last keeper, Osgood, served to 1917. Editor should check the 1970 entry's source before changing it.
The light was first lit in 1871 (LHF, NPS, USLHS). The 1983 event is a relight after restoration.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NRHP form gives 1870 construction for $3,000 in its chronology, but 1877 in its significance statement. LHF and NPS show the range in operation January 1871 and the brick tower finished in spring 1871. Story states first lighting in 1871 and says the construction date is disputed.

notes_for_editor: 1) Construction date: NRHP chronology 1870 ($3,000) vs NRHP significance statement 1877; LHF and NPS say the range went into operation January 1871. The story says the dates are disputed. 2) Removal from the site: NRHP says 1966 ('became part of the Salem Maritime Historic Site'), LHF says 1979. Both are footnoted and stated. 3) Status: the record says 'active' but the USLHS record says 'Active Aid to Navigation? No' (Private Aid: Yes). NPS says the solar light flashes red every six seconds. Not changed; check with the Coast Guard Light List. 4) Structure height: the record's 4.0 m tower height conflicts with NPS (about 20 ft to the top of the cupola, about 6.1 m) and NRHP (25 ft above high water, which the story gives). Not changed. 5) Lens sequence after 1901 (LHF: 4th 1904, 6th 1910) is not checked against Board reports; the local corpus holds Board reports only to 1901. The Wikipedia lens sequence is not used. 6) The 1914 fire account rests on LHF only; Chronicling America searches for 'Derby Wharf' and 'Osgood' in 1914 returned HTTP 520 errors from loc.gov and no usable hits. 7) Mrs. Osgood is not named in the story beyond 'Mrs. Osgood'; she is listed as 'other' in the record with her first name not given. 8) The Commissioner's OCR list (fiscal 1918) prints 'Salem' as '8alem' and changes as 'CHANOED'. The Derby entry sits under the heading 'Fiscal Year 1918'; the printed page 31 and scan page 345 were confirmed with corpus.py page. 9) The Board's railing entry is under 'FISCAL YEAR ENDED JUNE 30, 1892' (scan 389, confirmed with corpus.py page). The Bulletin index entry (Derby Wharf, change in illuminant, 292) is on index PDF page 13 (confirmed with corpus.py grep). 10) The 1,190 square feet figure: LHF prints '1190 ½ square feet' with the half lost to OCR-like damage ('1190 �'); the story writes 1,190½ and the evidence quote covers only '1190'. 11) Access: LHF says 'Grounds open, tower closed'; NPS and USLHS say 'Open to Public: No'. The story states the disagreement; the access level is 'restricted' (partial access: grounds per LHF, tower closed). 12) The NRHP form is dated 1981 but its chronology carries a 1983 relight entry (as printed); the story attributes the relight to the form's chronology. 13) Length: 961 words in six chapters. Each chapter has sourced material, but the text is below the 1,200-word band for the rich shape in research/STORY_GUIDE.md; it was not padded. The owner or the writer may condense it to four chapters. 14) Metre conversions added to the story's US measures (800 m, 111 m², 6.1 m, 7.6 m); they are arithmetic, not sourced claims. 15) No photos added; the NPS photo credit and LHF photos are not mirrored.
